title: Prepare for removal of S4 classes `standardGeneric` and `nonstandardGeneric`
description: It is planned that R 4.7.0 will prune S4 classes `standardGeneric` and `nonstandardGeneric` and their subclasses, so that all new S4 generic function objects *have* class `genericFunction` rather than inheriting from that class indirectly.  Note that the to-be-pruned S4 classes are documented as for internal use by package **methods**, hence *not* for use by any contributed package.  This PR guards your package against the pending change in R by eliminating usage of the to-be-pruned S4 classes while preserving existing behaviour.

title: Updates outdated instruction in manual (small fix)
description: I love this package. Typing `?conflicted` instructs users to use assignment to fix conflicts. That's outdated. Other parts of the package suggest `conflict_prefer()`. This human-written pull request makes a tiny change to update `conflicted-package.Rd`.

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to conflicted website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the conflicted website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Refer to canonical pacakge in case of duplicates
description:
This also deals with the case where two packages import from a third package, and a fourth package overwrites it.

Will add tests.

Closes #93.

## Example

``` r
library(conflicted)
library(plyr)
library(dm)
library(mcmcdata)

mutate
#> Error:
#> ! [conflicted] mutate found in 2 packages.
#> Either pick the one you want with `::`:
#> • dplyr::mutate
#> • plyr::mutate
#> Or declare a preference with `conflicts_prefer()`:
#> • `conflicts_prefer(dplyr::mutate)`
#> • `conflicts_prefer(plyr::mutate)`
#> Backtrace:
#>     ▆
#>  1. └─conflicted (local) `<fn>`()
#>  2.   └─cli::cli_abort(...) at conflicted/R/disambiguate.R:51:4
#>  3.     └─rlang::abort(...)
```

title: Handle conflicts involving primitive functions
description:
This is to address issues #46 and #48.

The current behaviour is that when a package exports a function that masks a primitive function, this conflict is not detected by `conflicted`. e.g. if we run 

```
library(conflicted)
library(greta)
```

then `greta::gamma` masks `base::gamma`, and `conflicted` will not force the user to make a deliberate choice.

The cause of this behaviour is that `conflict_scout` calls `is_superset` (via `superset_principle`) to check whether the formals of the function exported by the package are a superset of the formals of the base function of the same name, in which case the conflict is ignored. This breaks down if the base version of the function is a primitive, since primitives don't have formals, and so we get an error from `rlang::fn_fmls`.

The proposed behaviour is that conflicts involving primitives should be the same from the user's perspective as conflicts involving non-primitive base functions, e.g.      

```
library(conflicted)
library(greta)
```

should result in the user being forced to choose whether they want `greta::gamma` or `base::gamma` when they call `gamma`. This is achieved by explicitly checking whether the base function is a primitive and returning FALSE from `is_superset` if it is.
